title: Quality and recording
summary: Evaluation forms, calibration, coaching, recording policies, and the prerequisites for AI scoring.

lessons.title: Quality management evaluates the conversation
lessons.summary: QM records and scores interactions, and it can coach. It is not the schedule.
paras: The quality article describes evaluation forms, policies, calibration, coaching, disputes, and the ability to evaluate in-progress or recorded interactions. Speech and text analytics can cover the conversations so a form is not the only way you learn what was said. Screen recording is a separate capability for the agent’s screen during ACD interactions.

The 2023 feature-matrix summary showed quality on the packages that include it, and the current overview puts that quality layer on CX 2 and above. WFM remains CX 3. Do not tell a CX 2 customer they have scheduling because they have evaluations.

lessons.title: Forms have questions and weights
lessons.summary: The form is the rubric. Weights decide which questions move the score.
paras: The QM article points at evaluation form weights and at creating forms. A form that weights greeting at 80 percent and resolution at 5 percent will congratulate short polite calls that do not solve the problem. AI scoring, later, can answer some questions only when the interaction is transcribed and you have the tokens. The rubric still has to be one a human accepts.

Calibration is how you find out that two evaluators do not mean the same thing by “empathy.” The article lists calibration as its own activity. Skipping it makes the leaderboard a measure of who graded, not of what happened.

figure.caption: Weights decide the score. Calibration decides the graders agree.

lessons.title: Recording policies choose calls and retention
lessons.summary: A policy decides which ACD calls are recorded and how long they are kept. A secure flow is a hole in a segment, not a substitute for the policy.
paras: About recording says you use policies to choose ACD calls and retention, and that a user can also record their own calls. Screen recording is specifically the agent’s screen during ACD interactions. Retention is a legal and a storage question. Storage is also a fair-use meter. Keep the policy’s duration and the fair-use page in the same review.

A secure payment flow stops recording for that entry. It does not set retention for the rest of the call. QM cannot evaluate audio you never recorded. If the policy records nothing, the form has nothing to play.

figure.caption: Policy selects the call. Retention decides how long it lives.

lessons.title: Coaching and disputes close the loop
lessons.summary: A score that the agent cannot see and cannot dispute is not a quality program.
paras: The QM article lists coaching appointments, evaluation disputes, and managing those disputes. It also lists monitoring and coaching in-progress interactions. The point of the form is a conversation with the agent. A hidden score changes nothing on the next call.

Disputes are not a failure of the form. They are how you find a bad question or a bad grade. Calibration feeds the same loop. If every dispute is denied in a minute, agents will stop reading the form.

lessons.title: AI scoring needs STA, QM, and tokens
lessons.summary: The FAQ is blunt: AI scoring requires Speech and Text Analytics, Quality Management, and AI Experience Tokens.
paras: The STA FAQ says AI scoring needs the interaction transcribed, and that Virtual Supervisor AI scoring needs STA, QM, and AI Experience Tokens. It also says one token covers 20 evaluations analyzed with AI scoring. Agent Copilot summaries are not billed a second time when Virtual Supervisor shows the same summary. Those are billing rules, and the FAQ is the source. Re-read the token ratio before you model a budget. This sentence is a pointer, not a quote you should freeze if the FAQ changes.
AI scoring answers form questions. It does not replace calibration. A model that grades a question your form defines badly will do it consistently and wrongly. Fix the question.

lessons.title: Retention, export, and the reason you recorded
lessons.summary: Export and AWS recording paths exist so a recording can leave the platform under a policy, not as a side copy.
paras: The QM article mentions AWS recording export among the tools around evaluations. About recording points at related articles for listening and for S3-style recording paths. Any export is still personal data. The fair-use storage meter and your retention policy decide how long the original lives. An export bucket you never expire is a second retention policy you forgot to write.
Do not export “for a demo” from a production queue. Use a lab queue and a lab policy. The recordings in this lab’s incidents are synthetic text, not audio from a person.

figure.caption: Export is a second copy. It needs its own retention.
